The main takeaway from our work is that

SCP should seek to understand how local communities are already supporting high forest cover, rather than proposing reserves in the same places where community-based social processes are supporting conservation.

SCP exercises should not be used as a justification for the creation of new public protected areas in a region that already conserves its own forests, and that SCP exercises should be informed by the local context.

SCP exercises need to be informed by local community knowledge, history, and social processes, and that the best conservation plans will be those that build on existing local conservation initiatives.
